subject: history_social
passage: The dry zone of ancient Sri Lanka supported cities such as Anuradhapura through a vast system of reservoirs, known locally as tanks, and the channels that linked them. Some tanks, built under royal sponsorship, covered many square kilometers. Historian Nimal Jayawardena argues that so extensive a system could only have been planned and maintained by a powerful central state, which organized labor and decided how water was shared across the countryside.
passage_b: The great royal reservoirs were indeed state projects. But most of the dry zone's tanks were small village reservoirs arranged in cascades along shallow valleys, each catching the overflow of the one above it. Records of local water rights suggest that these tanks were added a few at a time over generations and that villages themselves maintained them and divided their water. The system as a whole may owe as much to accumulated local effort as to central planning.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument made by Jayawardena in Text 1?

choices.A: By denying that any of Sri Lanka's ancient reservoirs were built under royal sponsorship
choices.B: By arguing that it overlooks the many small tanks that villages built and ran themselves
choices.C: By claiming that the village cascades held more water than the great royal reservoirs did
choices.D: By agreeing that the cascades reflect central planning while doubting the royal tanks' size

explanation.why: Text 2 agrees that "the great royal reservoirs were indeed state projects," but it points out that "most of the dry zone's tanks" were village reservoirs that villages "themselves maintained." It concludes that the system "may owe as much to accumulated local effort as to central planning." Text 2 would say Jayawardena's "only" claim ignores this local part of the system.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 accepts that the great reservoirs were state projects.
explanation.B: Correct. Text 2 argues that most tanks were village works, built gradually and managed locally, which Jayawardena's account of a centrally run system leaves out.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 compares the number of village tanks, not how much water they held.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 credits the cascades to local effort, not central planning, and never questions the size of the royal tanks.
